title: Fast-path sprintlet checklist and telemetry log — May 2024 (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, repeatable checklist for a "sprintlet" release: a narrow-scope, fast-path production push designed to land small performance or routing fixes with minimal blast radius. It combines a preflight checklist, an hourly rollout calendar for a 36-hour window, telemetry thresholds, and a short post-release notes template.

Context / When to use:
- Narrow code changes that affect routing, batching heuristics, or tiered model fallbacks.
- Expected user-visible impact < 0.5% of total traffic per cohort.
- Goal: land fix, validate telemetry for 24 hours, graduate to normal cadence or roll back.

Owners & Roster (primary/backup):
- Release lead: Liam Chen / backup: Aisha Kapoor
- Observability lead: Marta Ruiz / backup: Ethan Park
- Infra engineer (cutover & rollback): Ravi Patel / backup: Open
- QA: Ethan Park (smoke test owner)
- Communications: Aisha Kapoor (Slack + release note)

Preflight (two working days before preferred, but can compress to 4 hours for urgent sprintlets):
- [ ] Confirm PR merged to release branch and no migrations (PR: #112).
- [ ] Run quick canary tests in staging: latency p95 within +10% of baseline, error rate < 0.2%. (owner: QA)
- [ ] Validate model artifact hash and quantization profile (owner: Infra).
- [ ] Ensure rollout playbook updated (this doc) and team pagers on-call aware. Post link to #release-watch.
- [ ] Add feature flag + canary route config to enable 1% circuits in prod (config PR id noted).
- [ ] Confirm telemetry dashboards & alerts are active: latency, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, queue length, downstream retry rate.
- [ ] Prepare quick rollback snapshot: deployment manifest + last-known-good config saved in S3 (s3 path: s3://redwood-release-snapshots/2024-05-03-sprintlet).

Cutover timeline (Target window: 36 hours; suggested start: 09:00 UTC on low-traffic day)
T-60 to T-15 min: final sync
- 09:00 UTC: pre-launch check-in, confirm all owners present in video/Slack.
- 09:10: re-run staging smoke once more, attach logs to PR.
- 09:20: enable feature flag in experiment control to route 0.1% traffic.
- 09:30: monitor 30 minutes for initial signal, then increment to 1% at 10:00.

T0+ (first 6 hours): gradual ramp and tight observation
- 10:00: ramp to 1% (canary cohort A).
- 10:15: quick smoke tests against live canary cohort.
- 10:30-12:00: telemetry watch. If no adverse signals, proceed.
- 12:00: ramp to 5% (cohort B).
- 14:00: ramp to 20% if all green (cohort C).
- 18:00: evaluate for wider release or hold overnight at 20% to observe night traffic patterns.

T0+ (24–36 hours): observe and decide
- 24h: Observability lead to present telemetry summary and recommend: graduate to 100% routing, keep at 20% for another 24h, or rollback.
- 36h: Final decision checkpoint. If no decision or major regressions, default to rollback and open incident review.

Smoke test list (run at each ramp step):
- [ ] Basic generation: 20 short prompts sample, compare median latency to baseline (< +15%).
- [ ] Long prompt stress: 5 long-form prompts (2–3k tokens) should not increase error rate.
- [ ] Streaming integrity: ensure partial response streaming continues without truncation.
- [ ] Embedding sanity-check: compare sample vector similarity against baseline set.
- [ ] Auth & quota paths: validate token-limited requests still enforced.

Telemetry thresholds (auto-escalate if breached):
- Error rate (5xx + client-facing errors) absolute increase > 0.3 percentage points OR relative increase > 200% -> Page SRE + rollback candidate.
- Latency: p95 increase > 50% sustained for 10 minutes -> Alert @observability + consider pause.
- GPU utilization: sudden sustained drop > 30% across nodes (possible misrouting) -> Investigate.
- Queue growth: enqueue length increasing by >2x baseline for 15+ minutes -> Scale or rollback.
- Retry amplification: downstream retry rate increase > 50% -> hold and diagnose.

Rollback decision matrix (quick rules):
- Critical user-facing error spike (as above) within first 6 hours -> immediate rollback to LKG (last-known-good) + postmortem.
- Latency regression with severe business impact (p95 > 2x baseline) -> pause ramp and revert changes causing the regression.
- Non-critical telemetry flakiness -> hold at current percentage and open ticket for deeper analysis (REL-2024).

Rollback procedure (infra owner primary):
- [ ] Disable feature flag immediately (0% routing).
- [ ] Re-deploy snapshot manifest from s3://redwood-release-snapshots/2024-05-03-sprintlet with one-click script: ./scripts/rollback.sh --manifest 2024-05-03
- [ ] Validate smoke tests pass on LKG traffic.
- [ ] Notify stakeholders in #release-watch and update Jira (REL-2024) with status and preliminary root cause.

Observability artifacts to capture (append to this doc):
- Dashboard snapshots (links) at t=0, t=+6h, t=+24h, t=+36h.
- Sample request traces for failing requests (attach trace IDs).
- Aggregated logs for the canary cohorts.
- Perf profile of model worker nodes if latency changes.

Post-release notes (template) — fill and publish when status = Graduated or Rolled back:
- Release ID: sprintlet-2024-05-03-XX
- Owner: Liam Chen (release lead)
- Scope: one-line description of change (config/tuning/fix)
- Cohorts: A=1%, B=5%, C=20%
- Start time: 2024-05-03 10:00 UTC
- Outcome: Graduated / Rolled back (pick one)
- Key metrics observed: p95 latency change, error delta, GPU utilization summary
- Follow-ups: list of tickets, action owners, timeline for full rollout if graduated

Open questions & TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm which downstream services need synthetic load during night observation — @Marta to confirm.
- [ ] Add a lightweight regression test for the new batching heuristic in CI (small PR).
- [ ] Consider automating 2-step ramp with a deploy pipeline that can roll back automatically on threshold breach (engineering cost estimate needed).

Notes / field observations from last dry-run (2024-04-18):
- Minor spike in client errors when routing hit 5% for a noisy tenant; identified missing rate-limit header handling in the fallback path. Patch was small but highlights need for 2-tiered smoke coverage.
- Observability lag: dashboard refresh was 20–30s, increased time-to-decision. Need to reduce aggregation window during sprintlets.

Append: quick commands & links (operational clipboard)
- Rollback script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/deploy-scripts/blob/main/rollback.sh
- Staging smoke job: ./ci/run-staging-smoke.sh --subset sprintlet
- Snapshot store: s3://redwood-release-snapshots/2024-05-03-sprintlet
- Jira ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/REL-2024

If you run this sprintlet, paste telemetry snapshots and a short 2–3 line debrief under this doc (append). Keep it terse — the goal is fast learning and reproducibility.

-- end of draft --

(Notes: this is intentionally compact and checklist-driven. It's a working doc; please edit inline. If we adopt widely, we'll promote to canonical Confluence page and link from release runbooks.)
